hook.line: Tomás is telling Mariana about the people and places that matter in his new life: the building, the friends, the man he talked to yesterday. English lets you finish with a little word, like the building I was born in. Spanish won't. It moves that word to the front.
hook.es: Este es el edificio en el que nació mi abuela.
hook.en: This is the building my grandmother was born in.

examples.es: Es el edificio en el que nació mi abuela.
examples.en: It's the building my grandmother was born in.

examples.es: La persona a quien le escribí no contestó.
examples.en: The person I wrote to didn't answer.

examples.es: Los amigos con los que vivo son de Cali.
examples.en: The friends I live with are from Cali.

examples.es: El hombre con quien hablé es el dueño.
examples.en: The man I spoke with is the owner.

examples.es: Es el parque del que te hablé.
examples.en: It's the park I told you about.

examples.es: Esta es la calle por la que pasa el bus.
examples.en: This is the street the bus goes along.

examples.es: El café en el que trabajo es de Rosa.
examples.en: The café I work in is Rosa's.

rule:
In English the little word can hang at the end: the friends I live *with*. In Spanish it always comes first, in front of the thing you're describing: *los amigos con los que vivo*.

The pattern is little word + *el / la / los / las* + *que*. The article matches the thing you're describing:
*la casa en la que vivo*
*los amigos con los que vivo*

For people you can use *quien* instead, which doesn't change for gender: *el hombre con quien hablé*, *la persona a quien escribí*.

*A* plus *el* is *al*, *de* plus *el* is *del*: *el lugar al que voy*, *el parque del que te hablé*.

For a place, *donde* still works.
smallPrint: Teachers call this a relative clause with a preposition. Spanish never leaves the preposition stranded at the end.

readAndPick.es: La casa en la que vivo es vieja.
options: The house I live in is old.
The houses I live in are old.

readAndPick.es: Los amigos con los que vivo son de Cali.
options: The friend I live with is from Cali.
The friends I live with are from Cali.

readAndPick.es: La persona a quien le escribí no contestó.
options: The person who wrote to me didn't answer.
The person I wrote to didn't answer.

readAndPick.es: El parque del que te hablé es grande.
options: The park I told you about is big.
The park that told you is big.
The park I'm from is big.

readAndPick.es: El lugar al que voy es muy bonito.
options: The place I'm coming from is very pretty.
The place I'm going to is very pretty.

readAndPick.es: Las vecinas con las que hablo son de Cali.
options: The neighbours (women) I talk to are from Cali.
The neighbour (a woman) I talk to is from Cali.

readAndPick.es: Esta es la calle por la que pasa el bus.
options: This is the bus I take along the street.
This is the street the bus goes along.

readAndPick.es: La persona para quien trabajo es la dueña.
options: The person I work with is the owner.
The person I work for is the owner.

readAndPick.es: El hombre con quien hablé es el dueño.
options: The man I spoke with is the owner.
The man who spoke to me is the owner.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *en el que* or *en la que* and type the whole sentence: Es la casa ___ vivo.
yourTurn.answer: Es la casa en la que vivo.
yourTurn.why: *Casa* is feminine, so the article is *la*: *en la que*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *con quien* or *quien con* and type the whole sentence: El hombre ___ hablé es el dueño.
yourTurn.answer: El hombre con quien hablé es el dueño.
accept: El hombre con el que hablé es el dueño.
yourTurn.why: The little word goes first: *con quien*, never at the end.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: The person I wrote to didn't answer.
yourTurn.answer: La persona a quien le escribí no contestó.
accept: La persona a la que le escribí no contestó.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: It's the building my grandmother was born in.
yourTurn.answer: Es el edificio en el que nació mi abuela.
accept: Es el edificio donde nació mi abuela.
yourTurn.why: *En* goes in front of *el que*, matching the masculine *edificio*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: The friends I live with are from Cali.
yourTurn.answer: Los amigos con los que vivo son de Cali.
accept: Los amigos con quienes vivo son de Cali.
yourTurn.why: Friends is plural, so *con los que*, or *con quienes*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say to a friend: It's the park I told you about.
yourTurn.answer: Es el parque del que te hablé.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it plural: La casa en la que vivo es vieja.
yourTurn.answer: Las casas en las que vivo son viejas.
yourTurn.why: The articles and the adjective all follow the plural houses, and *es* becomes *son*.

pitfalls.wrong: La persona que hablé con es el dueño.
pitfalls.right: La persona con quien hablé es el dueño.
pitfalls.why: Almost. Spanish can't end on *con*: put it first, then *quien* or *la que*.

pitfalls.wrong: La casa en el que vivo es vieja.
pitfalls.right: La casa en la que vivo es vieja.
pitfalls.why: The article follows the thing you're describing, and *casa* is feminine.

pitfalls.wrong: El hombre con que hablé es el dueño.
pitfalls.right: El hombre con quien hablé es el dueño.
pitfalls.why: After a preposition you need an article or *quien*, not a bare *que*.

personal: Tell me about someone you work or study with, or a place you spend time in. Use *con quien* or *en el que* (or *la que*).
